content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm having trouble with my [product_name] [version_no]. While I can successfully connect to the router, register the device, and deploy to the cloud using [product_name] [product_name], controlling a bit from the web page doesn't work. When I set the bit from a [product_name] panel connected to the device, I can observe the change in the device's shadow on AWS. Despite checking all connections, reviewing the program and permissions in AWS, everything appears correct, but communication from the cloud web page built in [product_name] [product_name] to the device fails. The AWS permissions applied are: AWSIoTFullAccess, AdministratorAccess-AWSElasticBeanstalk, and AWSElasticBeanstalkReadOnly. I watched a video tutorial and noticed the only difference is they're using the Tomcat platform version 4.1.4 while mine is 4.2.13, which AWS sets by default and cannot be changed.
I've resolved the issue! The problem was with the AWS region; I registered 'us-east1' on AWS and 'us-east2' in [product_name].

Was the region mix-up the only problem? I'm experiencing similar issues. I've checked that the regions match, and everything seems correct. The device shadow appears on AWS, and the project deploys successfully, but there's no communication between the [product_name] and the web interface. Additionally, AWS shows the environment as 'deprecated.'

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering difficulties connecting and operating [product_name] hardware through AWS Cloud using [product_name] cloud editor tools. Although device registration and cloud deployment succeed, attempts to interact remotely from the custom web interface fail to affect the hardware state. Frustration centers around troubleshooting steps that do not resolve communication failures, with region mismatches cited as a significant technical issue. Some users also notice deprecated environments in their AWS setup, which adds complexity.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable and straightforward communication between their [product_name] hardware and custom cloud web interfaces. They want changes made through the cloud to seamlessly synchronize and reflect on the physical device, with clear documentation and dependable configuration.
